notes.meaning: God told Elijah that the long drought was coming to an end. After more than two years living hidden at Zarephath, Elijah was commanded to go and show himself to King Ahab. The Lord promised that He would send rain back upon the land.
Elijah set out at once to meet Ahab, showing great courage by obeying God even though the king was hunting for his life. In the capital city of Samaria, the famine was growing worse every day.
Ahab called for Obadiah, the man in charge of managing the royal palace. Even though Obadiah worked for an evil king, he deeply respected and worshiped the true God in his heart.

When Queen Jezebel tried to kill all the Lord's prophets, Obadiah risked his life to protect them. He hid one hundred prophets in two caves, fifty in each, and secretly supplied them with food and water to keep them alive.

Ahab ordered Obadiah to search every spring and valley in the land for patches of green grass. The king was desperate to keep his horses and mules alive so he would not lose his valuable royal livestock and chariot teams.
The king and his palace manager divided the territory between them to search every corner. Ahab rode off in one direction by himself, and Obadiah went in another direction by himself.
As Obadiah traveled along his route, Elijah suddenly appeared before him. Recognizing the prophet, Obadiah bowed low with his face to the ground in deep respect and greeted him.
Elijah told him plainly that it was indeed him. He then commanded Obadiah to go back to his master Ahab and announce that Elijah was here.
Obadiah was terrified by this order and asked what wrong he had done to deserve such danger. He believed that taking this message would surely cause Ahab to execute him.

Obadiah explained that Ahab had sent search parties to every surrounding nation and kingdom looking for Elijah. Whenever a country reported that Elijah was not there, Ahab forced their leaders to swear an oath that they were telling the truth.
After describing that frantic search, Obadiah could not understand why Elijah was now telling him to go and announce his presence to Ahab.

Obadiah worried that as soon as he left, the Spirit of the Lord would miraculously sweep Elijah away to another hiding place. If Ahab arrived and found no Elijah, he would assume Obadiah lied to him and have him killed. Obadiah pleaded that he had faithfully served the Lord ever since he was young.
Obadiah asked Elijah if he had not heard what he did when Queen Jezebel was killing God's prophets. He reminded him how he had hidden one hundred prophets in caves and fed them through the famine.
Because of that extreme danger, Obadiah repeated his dread of carrying the prophet's message. He feared once more that if Elijah vanished, the king would take his life.
Elijah reassured Obadiah by making a solemn promise in the name of the living Lord of Hosts, whom he served. He gave his word that he would definitely stand before Ahab that very day.
Relying on Elijah's solemn oath, Obadiah went straight to Ahab and delivered the news. Upon hearing the message, Ahab turned around to go and meet the prophet.

When Ahab came face to face with Elijah, he tried to intimidate him by asking if he was the troubler of Israel. Ahab blamed Elijah and his announcement for causing the devastating drought and national misery.

Elijah boldly rejected the charge and told the king that Ahab and his royal family were the real troublemakers. They had abandoned the commandments of the Lord and led the nation into worshiping the false Canaanite gods known as the Baals.

Elijah took charge and ordered Ahab to gather all the people of Israel to Mount Carmel. He also demanded the presence of the 450 prophets of Baal and the 400 prophets of Asherah who were supported by Queen Jezebel.
Ahab complied with the prophet's demand and sent word across Israel. The people assembled on Mount Carmel along with the prophets of Baal to witness the showdown.

Elijah stood before the crowd and asked how long they would limp back and forth between two sides, like someone stumbling between two opinions. He challenged them to follow the Lord if He is the true God, or to follow Baal if Baal is god. Confronted with their divided loyalty, the people did not say a single word.
Elijah pointed out the stark contrast in numbers before the crowd. He stood as the only prophet of the Lord present to speak publicly, while Baal had 450 prophets standing on his side.

Elijah set the rules for a fair public test by asking for two young bulls. He gave Baal's prophets first choice of an animal to slaughter, chop into pieces, and place on the wood without setting fire to it, while he promised to prepare the other bull the exact same way.
